target.title: fix(browser): check existing-session wait navigation [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running browser control against an existing Chrome session could receive a successful wait response even when the wait action moved the selected tab to a URL that should be rejected by the configured browser navigation policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing-session wait actions now use the same post-interaction navigation guard as the other existing-session interaction paths. This keeps wait conditions, URL waits, and function-backed waits on one policy-checking path without changing Playwright-backed browser actions.

## User Impact

Browser control behavior is more consistent across existing-session action kinds. Wait actions now return the same kind of policy failure as sibling interactions when the resulting tab state is not allowed by the current browser configuration.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts --reporter=verbose` - 18 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.existing-session.test.ts --reporter=verbose` - 14 tests passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

Known limitation: remote Testbox proof could not start in this session because neither the Crabbox nor Blacksmith CLI was installed on PATH and no sibling Crabbox binary was available.
